sentence: > The jealousy reading and the future-reader reading of Sappho fragment 31, as developed, give competing accounts of what organizes the same five features: the one seated opposite (a rival, or an occupant of an open seat), the addressee (a beloved woman present, or the voice being received), the object of the distress (the pair, or the scene of her own reception), the colour (pallor with fear supplied, or the body passing to the dried sheet), and the agentless dare (the speaker's, or the receiver's).

sentence: Its sharpest instance is a single poem: what Sappho 31 is, a woman undone or a maker inscribing her reader, is decided in this journal, by conviction, in a report no one outside could read, and the reading it keeps was filed, never argued (I.4a).
